chapter: Gulf Coast and later working bands
title: Gulf Coast hotel and nightclub jobs and cheating waiters
summary: Hirsch played Gulf Coast hotels for $17.50 a week plus food, and tells of two waiters who raised checks and robbed a slot machine.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Did you play over on the Gulf Coast much in the early years? Oh yeah. You did? Spot jobs. Spot jobs. Who did you play over there mostly with? Pinky and Pete and Al Herrick. In the early years in the 30s. No. It's when we were kids when we got, we got a job over there at the hotels. So in the 20s.
In the 20s. In the 30s. We got a job over at the hotels. And Pete and Al Herg.
In the early years, in the 30s?

Well, not in the 30s. Oh, in the 30s. No, it's when we were kids when we got used to, we'd get a job over there at the hotels. In the 30s, we'd get a job over at the hotels. And you'd play the hotels for lunch and dinner, and you got $17.50 a week, plus food. And you'd work a nightclub, and we lived at the nightclub, and got crabs. Not the kind you eat. Not the kind you eat. And I think we used to get $25 a week for that. So, I mean, they used to give us a little night meal out there, and we slept there, and we played the hotel. That lasted about two weeks, I guess, at the most. I never will forget, there was two guys who were comedians and singers. They used to be songwriters. They were around New Orleans a long time. I forget their names. But they were also waiters. And in those days, the Gulf Coast was very, very cheap. Very cheap. I mean, you'd feel that you paid $5 for a dinner in Chicago. They'd charge you a dollar for a dinner down here. So these guys, they went in business for themselves, and they had a whole set of new checks made. And every time somebody gets for a check for their meal, they didn't get a check that came from the kitchen. They got their checks that they made out themselves. Raised every check, about $8, $10, and they were in business for themselves. So they paid a check for the kitchen for about $2, and they got $8 for the check. So they were six bucks a head. But these guys, I mean, they were really manipulators. And then I'll never forget one night, they didn't get the, they weren't getting paid their money. So they took the, after the place closed, they went and got a hammer and broke the glass on the jackpot on the slot machine and took the quarters out of that. Oh, they were dangerous.
